newsitem.title: CHILE: No new sign of Canadian yachtsman lost in Pacific.
newsitem.headline: No new sign of Canadian yachtsman lost in Pacific.

text.p: Chilean rescuers found no new sign of a lone Canadian yachtsman lost in the Pacific in an around-the-world race after picking up a radio signal which may have come from him, the navy said on Friday.

The Chilean navy stepped up air searches for the sailor, Gerry Roufs, after a military plane picked up a brief radio signal -- but no visual sign -- from a ship in the Pacific about 100 miles (160 km) northwest of Cape Horn.

The ship's skipper said he was sailing west of the cape and was understood to identify his vessel as Group LH -- which sounds like the name of Roufs' yacht, Group LG2, but neither navy spokesmen nor race organisers would venture to say if it was the same boat.
The plane lost radio contact before the skipper was able to identify himself further. Searches yielded no new sign of Roufs, the navy said.
"The search has not had positive results so far," said a statement from the navy.
Roufs was part of the Vendee Globe around-the-world race. He disappeared somewhere between New Zealand, Chile and Antarctica in an area known for treacherous seas and currents.
The navy said race organisers informed them of Roufs' last known position, 1,500 nautical miles west of Cape Horn, on Wednesday and that the navy began looking for him.

The radio signal raised the prospect that Roufs had managed to sail 1,400 miles (2,040 km) across the South Pacific without being detected by satellite radar, search planes and ships of various nationalities.
"There was no visual contact at all. It was just a radio contact and it was, unfortunately, very brief," said a navy spokesman in the far-south port of Punta Arenas.
The Australian navy looked for Roufs after rescuing two other racers, and an Indian freighter gave up its search on Wednesday after 24 hours.
The navy alerted all ships in the area and sent search planes to look for the yachtsman, said the statement.
